Cut and Edit page nonlinear editing and trimming

Node-based grading: serial nodes, layer nodes, and node caching
DaVinci YRGB and Color Managed workflows (RCM and CST)
Creative look development and shot matching

Basic Fusion Text+ titles and lower thirds
Deliver page mastering: standard Rec.709 SDR MP4/MOV exports

DaVinci Neural Engine advanced noise reduction (temporal and spatial)

Creating structured bin hierarchies: 01_Footage, 02_Audio, 03_Graphics, 04_Timelines
Creating metadata-driven Smart Bins (e.g. filtering by camera, frame rate, or resolution)
Clip coloring and metadata flags for fast visual identification in the timeline
Relinking moved media and locating missing directory paths
Troubleshooting offline media banners and permissions errors

lessons.why_it_matters: Systematic organization prevents missing file headaches during high-pressure color finishing.
lessons.expected_outcome: Professional Media Pool bin structure and metadata management.

lessons.what_is_taught: Containers and codecs: MP4 vs MOV wrappers, H.264, H.265, ProRes, and DNxHR, frame rates, resolution scaling, bit depth awareness (8-bit vs 10-bit), chroma subsampling (4:2:0 vs 4:2:2), source compatibility, and selecting optimized training media.
subtopics: Containers vs video codecs: understanding wrapper containers and compression streams
Broadcast and cinema codecs: Apple ProRes and Avid DNxHR editing formats
Delivery compression codecs: H.264 and H.265/HEVC web standards
Bit depth in colour grading: 8-bit banding risks vs 10-bit smooth color gradients
Chroma subsampling: 4:2:0 consumer compression vs 4:2:2 professional grading headroom
Operating system codec limitations in DaVinci Resolve Free (Windows vs macOS)
lessons.what_learner_does: Inspects clip metadata using Resolve's file inspector and verifies bit depth and chroma subsampling.
lessons.why_it_matters: Understanding bit depth prevents banding and contouring artifacts during aggressive grading.
lessons.expected_outcome: Technical comprehension of digital video containers, codecs, bit depths, and color headroom.

lessons.what_is_taught: Proxy workflows and optimized media: Proxy Media Generation, Blackmagic Proxy Generator app, proxy linking, Optimized Media formats, Render Cache modes (Smart vs User), playback performance tuning, and media storage planning.
subtopics: When to use proxies: editing 4K/60p footage smoothly on laptop and budget hardware
Generating proxies directly in the Media Pool using ProRes Proxy or DNxHR LB
The standalone Blackmagic Proxy Generator tool for background batch processing
Toggling Proxy Media playback on and off with a single menu command
Render Cache management: Smart Cache vs User Cache for node-heavy timelines
Managing disk space: purging stale render cache files to recover SSD storage
lessons.what_learner_does: Generates editing proxies for 4K media and verifies seamless full-resolution switching for grading.
lessons.why_it_matters: Proxy workflows allow smooth 24fps real-time playback even on modest hardware setups.
lessons.expected_outcome: Mastery of proxy generation, render caching, and disk storage management.

subtopics: Cut page vs Edit page: rapid rough-cut assembly vs precision non-linear finishing
Navigating dual-timeline views on the Cut page for fast scrubbing
Edit page anatomy: Source Viewer, Timeline Viewer, and Inspector properties
Track destination controls and auto-track selectors
Timeline navigation: timeline zoom, playhead snapping, and marker creation
Customizing keyboard shortcuts to match familiar industry standards
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a rough assembly on the Cut page and transitions it to the Edit page for refinement.
lessons.why_it_matters: Choosing the right page for each stage of post-production accelerates project turnaround.
lessons.expected_outcome: Fluent timeline construction across both Cut and Edit pages.

Importing XML, AAF, and EDL timeline interchange files
Relinking timeline clips to original high-resolution raw/log camera masters
Using an Offline Reference Movie with split-screen to verify frame-accurate conform
Resolving common conform errors: sizing shifts, speed change mismatches, and missing transitions

Exporting standalone project files (.drp) for team sharing
Creating complete DaVinci Resolve Project Archives (.dra) containing consolidated media

lessons.what_is_taught: Core nonlinear timeline editing on the Edit page: 3-point and 4-point editing, Source Viewer In/Out points, Insert and Overwrite edits, Append at End, track targeting, track locking, and essential keyboard editing shortcuts.
subtopics: Setting precise In and Out points in the Source Viewer (I and O shortcuts)
Three-point editing: Insert (F9) vs Overwrite (F10) vs Replace (F11)
Append at End (Shift+F12) for rapid sequence assembly
Track destination controls: directing audio and video to designated tracks
Keyboard shortcut mastery: J-K-L variable speed scrubbing and playback

Ripple edit: altering clip length while shifting all downstream timeline clips
Roll edit: adjusting the cut boundary between two clips without changing total duration
Slip edit: shifting the visible in/out window within a clip's underlying media
Slide edit: moving a clip along the timeline while rolling adjacent head and tail cuts
Precision frame nudging using the comma (,) and period (.) keys

lessons.why_it_matters: Trimming is where editing rhythm is sculpted; it transforms a rough cut into a tight story.

Maintaining spatial screen direction and understanding the 180-degree line
Dialogue continuity: covering awkward speech cuts using motivated B-roll cutaways
Reaction shots: using listener cutaways to add emotional weight to dialogue
Executing J-cuts: letting audio lead the visual cut to smooth dialogue transitions
Executing L-cuts: letting spoken audio trail over the incoming visual scene
lessons.what_learner_does: Assembles an interview sequence with seamless B-roll cutaways, J-cuts, and L-cuts.
lessons.why_it_matters: Continuity editing keeps viewers immersed in the narrative without noticing the cuts.

Curating interview soundbites: eliminating filler words and redundant phrases

Balancing interview narrative with visual B-roll storytelling
Structuring short-form commercial edits: hook, problem, solution, payoff, call to action

Managing client revision feedback and tracking change requests

Cleaning up timelines for the Color page: consolidating tracks and removing disabled clips
Decomposing compounds or nested clips when required for color access
Exporting an editorial review proxy with timecode window burn for stakeholder sign-off

lessons.what_is_taught: The core science and craft of color correction: technical correction vs artistic creative grading, exposure balance, white balance, contrast expansion, color casts, shot-to-shot consistency, and structured corrective workflow.
subtopics: Technical correction (normalizing reality) vs creative grading (sculpting artistic mood)
The human visual system: chromatic adaptation and optical illusions
Why uncorrected video looks washed out, muddy, or unnaturally tinted
The three pillars of technical balance: Exposure, Contrast, and White Balance
Identifying and neutralizing unwanted color casts from mixed lighting
The foundational sequence: establish black/white points before touching creative color
lessons.what_learner_does: Analyzes unbalanced footage clips and identifies exposure, contrast, and tint errors.
lessons.why_it_matters: Creative grades built on top of uncorrected, casted footage always fall apart across scene cuts.
lessons.expected_outcome: Clear distinction between technical correction and creative grading principles.

lessons.what_is_taught: Complete tour of the DaVinci Resolve Color page: Viewer, Node Editor, Gallery, Stills, Scopes, Primaries palettes (Wheels, Bars, Log), Curves, Qualifiers, Power Windows, Blur/Sharpen, Key, and Sizing palettes.
subtopics: Color page layout: Viewer, Node Graph, Gallery, and lower palette strip
Viewer display options: highlight mode, split screen, and reference wipe
Node Editor basics: creating serial nodes (Alt/Option+S) and labeling node functions
Gallery panel: grabbing stills (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+G) and organizing PowerGrades
Customizing the Color page UI for single-screen or dual-display grading
Essential keyboard shortcuts for colorists: bypass grade (Shift+D), loop, and still wipes
lessons.what_learner_does: Customizes the Color page workspace, creates labeled nodes, and grabs reference gallery stills.
lessons.why_it_matters: Fluid navigation of the Color page allows rapid experimentation without hunting through menus.
lessons.expected_outcome: Fluid navigation of Color page palettes, node graph, and viewer modes.

lessons.what_is_taught: Mastering technical video scopes: Waveform (Luma vs YC), RGB Parade, Vectorscope, and Histogram. Assessing exposure levels, shadow/highlight clipping, color channel balance, skin-tone line reference, and scope limitations.
subtopics: Reading the Waveform: measuring luminance from black (0 IRE) to peak white (1023 / 100 IRE)
RGB Parade: diagnosing color balance by comparing red, green, and blue channel heights
Vectorscope: reading hue angle and color saturation intensity
The Skin Tone Indicator line: evaluating skin pigment hue independent of ethnicity
Histogram: visualizing tonal pixel distribution across the dynamic range
Understanding scope limitations: why calibrated reference monitoring complements scopes
lessons.what_learner_does: Evaluates exposure, identifies color casts, and checks skin tone alignment using Waveform and Parade.
lessons.why_it_matters: Scopes provide objective mathematical truth; human eyes easily adapt and deceive the colorist.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to read and diagnose video scopes accurately for objective exposure and balance.

lessons.what_is_taught: Primary correction tools: Primaries Wheels (Lift, Gamma, Gain, Offset), Contrast, Pivot, Temperature, Tint, Saturation, Color Boost, Primaries Bars, and Custom Curves.
subtopics: Lift (shadows), Gamma (midtones), Gain (highlights), and Offset (global whole-image shift)
Adjusting master wheels vs color balance rings for each tonal range
Setting true black points with Lift and clean white points with Gain
Contrast and Pivot controls: expanding tonal contrast while anchoring midtones
Neutralizing color casts using Temperature (warm/cool) and Tint (green/magenta) sliders
Saturation vs Color Boost: boosting low-saturation pixels without over-saturating skin
lessons.what_learner_does: Neutralizes exposure, expands contrast, and balances color temperature on raw footage using primary wheels.
lessons.why_it_matters: Primary wheels are the workhorse of professional grading; 80% of color work occurs here.
lessons.expected_outcome: Mastery of Lift, Gamma, Gain, Offset, contrast pivot, and primary color balancing.

lessons.what_is_taught: Node architecture in DaVinci Resolve: Serial nodes, Parallel nodes, Layer nodes, node execution order, node labels, disabling nodes, node caching, and why node trees outperform linear layer stacks.
subtopics: Why nodes: non-linear signal processing vs destructive layer-based adjustment stacks
Serial nodes (Alt/Option+S): sequential signal flow from left to right
Parallel nodes (Alt/Option+P): applying independent adjustments simultaneously and blending
Layer nodes (Alt/Option+L): priority-based blending using blending modes or keys
Labeling nodes with specific descriptive names (e.g. 'Exp/Bal', 'Skin', 'Look')
Disabling single nodes (Ctrl/Cmd+D) or all nodes (Alt/Option+D) to compare before/after steps
lessons.what_learner_does: Constructs a clean 5-node serial and parallel grading tree with descriptive labels.
lessons.why_it_matters: Organized node trees allow precise adjustments without compounding errors or muddiness.
lessons.expected_outcome: Complete understanding of node signal flow, node types, and labeled organization.

lessons.what_is_taught: Building standard, repeatable node structures: input normalization node, primary exposure and balance node, contrast refinement node, secondary target nodes, creative look node, and output transform node.
subtopics: Designing a standardized production node tree template for commercial workflows
Node 01: Input Color Space Transform or Normalization (where needed)
Node 02: Primary Exposure & Balance (clean technical base)
Node 03: Contrast & Tonal Shape (establishing dynamic curve)
Node 04: Secondaries (isolated skin tones, skies, or brand colors)
Node 05: Creative Look / Palette (overall aesthetic grade)
Saving node structures to the Gallery as PowerGrades for instant reuse across clips
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds and applies a standardized 6-node grading structure across a multi-shot scene.
lessons.why_it_matters: Consistent node architecture makes team collaboration and client revisions effortless.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to construct and deploy structured, repeatable professional node trees.

lessons.what_is_taught: Secondary color correction: HSL Qualifiers, 3D Qualifier, selective color manipulation, HSL Curves (Hue vs Hue, Hue vs Sat, Hue vs Lum, Lum vs Sat, Sat vs Sat), skin-tone refinement, and avoiding unnatural edge artifacts.
subtopics: Secondary correction purpose: modifying specific colors without affecting the whole image
Sampling colors using the Qualifier eyedropper (Hue, Saturation, Luminance ranges)
Refining qualifier mattes: Clean Black, Clean White, Blur Radius, and In/Out Ratio
Using HSL Curves: Hue vs Hue (shifting skies), Hue vs Sat (desaturating background clutter)
Lum vs Sat: rolling off saturation in shadows and extreme highlights for photographic polish
Avoiding digital fringing, noise amplification, and unnatural boundary chatter
lessons.what_learner_does: Isolates a distracting colored object in the background and desaturates it cleanly using HSL curves.
lessons.why_it_matters: Secondary corrections allow colorists to direct viewer attention to key story elements.
lessons.expected_outcome: Proficiency in pulling clean qualifiers and utilizing HSL curves for selective adjustments.

lessons.what_is_taught: Spatial isolation using Power Windows: Linear, Circular, Polygon, and Curve windows, feathering parameters, window inversion, combining windows with qualifiers, the Window Tracker, and isolated exposure shaping.
subtopics: Power Window types: Linear (vignettes/graduated), Circular (faces), Curve (custom shapes)
Softening window boundaries: Inside/Outside feathering for invisible blend transitions
Inverting windows to affect everything outside the selected boundary
Tracking windows across moving subjects using Resolve's built-in Point/Cloud Tracker
Combining Power Windows with HSL Qualifiers to restrict color selections spatially
Lighting shaping: adding subtle vignettes and directional light accents to guide the viewer's eye
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates a tracked circular window over an actor's face, gently brightening exposure across a movement.
lessons.why_it_matters: Tracked Power Windows let colorists relight scenes digitally after shooting wraps.
lessons.expected_outcome: Mastery of Power Windows, edge feathering, and window tracking.

lessons.what_is_taught: Shot matching methodologies: grabbing gallery stills, using reference wipes (horizontal, vertical, mix), Split Screen modes, matching exposure across cuts, harmonizing white balance, matching contrast curves, and skin-tone continuity.
subtopics: The colorist's core mission: making shots filmed on different cameras/times match seamlessly
Grabbing stills (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+G) of the approved hero reference shot
Using Image Wipe (Ctrl/Cmd+W) to split the viewer between reference and target clips
Split Screen mode: viewing multiple timeline clips simultaneously side-by-side
Systematic matching order: match shadow level first, then highlight exposure, then midtone tint
Harmonizing skin tones across varying camera angles and lighting setups
lessons.what_learner_does: Matches three disparate camera angles from an interview scene to an approved hero reference shot.
lessons.why_it_matters: Shot matching is what makes a film look cohesive rather than an amateur compilation.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to match exposure, contrast, and color balance across multi-camera sequences.

lessons.what_is_taught: Identifying and resolving common grading pitfalls: crushed shadows with lost detail, clipped highlights, oversaturation, harsh contrast, unnatural or plastic skin tones, destructive LUT stacking, and inconsistent multi-shot contrast.
subtopics: Diagnosing crushed blacks (below 0 IRE) and blown highlights (clipped above 100 IRE)
The danger of oversaturation: neon color casts that clip on broadcast and mobile screens
Preserving natural skin texture: avoiding aggressive qualifiers that make skin look plastic
LUT stacking pitfalls: stacking multiple creative LUTs causing severe color banding and noise
Checking contrast consistency across dialogue cuts to avoid viewer visual fatigue
The Reset toolset: knowing when to wipe a node and start fresh with simpler adjustments
lessons.what_learner_does: Audits a poorly graded sequence, identifies 5 major color errors, and corrects them methodically.
lessons.why_it_matters: Avoiding technical errors ensures video passes broadcast and commercial platform quality control.
lessons.expected_outcome: Discipline in avoiding crushed tones, oversaturation, and unnatural skin artifacts.

lessons.what_is_taught: Step-by-step end-to-end grading session execution: footage inspection, color-management check, hero shot selection, primary balance, secondary refinement, shot matching pass, technical scope audit, and full-sequence playback review.
subtopics: Step 1: Inspecting source media, metadata, and color-management settings
Step 2: Selecting the hero shot that defines the visual benchmark for the scene
Step 3: Executing primary normalization, black/white balance, and contrast curve
Step 4: Applying secondary refinements (skin tones, sky enhancements, light shaping)
Step 5: Rippling or copying base grade to adjacent shots and matching variations
Step 6: Technical scope audit across all clips (checking RGB Parade and Waveform)
Step 7: Real-time playback review of the full sequence to verify flow and continuity
lessons.what_learner_does: Executes a complete grading session on a 6-shot scene from initial balance to final playback audit.
lessons.why_it_matters: A methodical step-by-step workflow ensures fast, repeatable, high-quality grading under client deadlines.
lessons.expected_outcome: Execution of a complete, professional, repeatable color grading session.

lessons.what_is_taught: Digital color science fundamentals: colour models, colour gamuts (Rec.709, DCI-P3, Rec.2020), gamma curves (Gamma 2.4, Gamma 2.2, sRGB), display-referred vs scene-referred workflows, dynamic range (stops), and mathematical color transforms.
subtopics: Understanding color spaces: chromaticity coordinates and visible spectral locus
Color gamuts: standard Rec.709 vs cinema DCI-P3 vs wide Rec.2020
Gamma transfer functions: encoding camera light intensity into display signals
Scene-referred (sensor light) vs display-referred (screen pixels) processing
Dynamic range in stops: from sensor capture to consumer display capabilities
How proper color science prevents clipping and hue shifts when expanding contrast
lessons.what_learner_does: Compares color gamuts on chromaticity charts and analyzes gamma curve responses.
lessons.why_it_matters: Color science literacy is what separates professional colorists from preset button-pushers.
lessons.expected_outcome: Solid theoretical understanding of color spaces, gamuts, gamma, and dynamic range.

lessons.what_is_taught: Camera Log encoding principles: why Log footage appears flat and desaturated, input colour-space identification (Sony S-Log3, Canon C-Log, Blackmagic Gen 5, Panasonic V-Log), camera metadata, correct normalization, and common conversion mistakes.
subtopics: Why cinema cameras record in Log: maximizing sensor dynamic range into memory
The optical illusion of Log: compressed shadows and highlights appearing low-contrast and milky
Identifying camera manufacturer color space and gamma from clip metadata
Major camera Log formats: Sony S-Gamut3.Cine/S-Log3, Canon Cinema Gamut/C-Log3, BMD Gen 5
The mistake of manual 'eyeball' normalization vs mathematical color transforms
Preventing crushed shadows and blown skies during camera log conversion
lessons.what_learner_does: Identifies camera Log profiles from raw media and normalizes clips mathematically.
lessons.why_it_matters: Incorrect Log conversion destroys highlights, distorts skin tones, and creates color noise.
lessons.expected_outcome: Accurate identification, handling, and mathematical normalization of camera Log footage.

lessons.what_is_taught: DaVinci Resolve Color Management (RCM): DaVinci YRGB vs DaVinci YRGB Color Managed, Color Science settings, Color Processing Mode (SDR vs HDR), Timeline working colour space (DaVinci Wide Gamut / Intermediate), Output colour space, tone mapping, and SDR workflow setup.
subtopics: DaVinci YRGB (standard unmanaged) vs DaVinci YRGB Color Managed (automated scene-referred)
Configuring RCM in Project Settings: Color Science and Timeline Color Space
DaVinci Wide Gamut (DWG) / DaVinci Intermediate: why grading in a massive color space is superior
Setting Output Color Space to Rec.709 / Gamma 2.4 for standard commercial SDR delivery
Automatic vs custom input color space assignment per clip in the Media Pool
Tone mapping options: DaVinci, Luminance, and Simple tone mapping algorithms
lessons.what_learner_does: Configures a project using DaVinci YRGB Color Managed with DWG/Intermediate timeline working space.
lessons.why_it_matters: RCM automatically normalizes multi-camera mixed Log footage into a unified, predictable space.
lessons.expected_outcome: Command of DaVinci Resolve Color Management setup and DWG/Intermediate working spaces.

lessons.what_is_taught: The Color Space Transform (CST) OFX plugin: node-based color transformations, Input Color Space & Input Gamma, Output Color Space & Output Gamma, Tone Mapping methods, correct CST placement in node trees, and avoiding duplicate transforms.
subtopics: Why CST is the most flexible color management tool in DaVinci Resolve Free
Applying CST to a node: selecting exact Input Color Space and Input Gamma
Setting Output Color Space to Rec.709 and Output Gamma to Gamma 2.4
Tone Mapping options: DaVinci tone mapping, Saturation Compression, and white point adaptation
The Sandwich CST workflow: CST In (Log to DWG) -> Grade Nodes -> CST Out (DWG to Rec.709)
Troubleshooting duplicate color space transforms that cause double-contrast clipping
lessons.what_learner_does: Builds a sandwich node pipeline using Color Space Transform plugins on raw camera Log clips.
lessons.why_it_matters: CST gives colorists surgical, per-node control over transforms without global project locks.
lessons.expected_outcome: Fluency in applying, configuring, and structuring Color Space Transform node workflows.

lessons.what_is_taught: Delivering for standard Rec.709 SDR displays: Rec.709 color gamut, Gamma 2.4 (broadcast/dark room) vs Gamma 2.2 (bright room/web), macOS QuickTime color management awareness, output consistency, and viewing environment limitations.
subtopics: Rec.709: the global standard display-referred broadcast and web video color space
Gamma choices: Gamma 2.4 for controlled studio viewing vs Gamma 2.2 for typical computer screens
The infamous macOS 'QuickTime gamma shift' explained and how to manage export tags
Viewing environment standards: neutral grey walls, controlled ambient lighting (D65 bias lighting)
The reality of consumer displays: why every phone, tablet, and TV looks slightly different
Relying on calibrated scopes as the objective benchmark rather than uncalibrated computer monitors
lessons.what_learner_does: Calibrates export color tags for Rec.709 Gamma 2.4 and evaluates on multiple viewing devices.
lessons.why_it_matters: Rec.709 SDR is the format in which 99% of commercial client work is viewed and evaluated.
lessons.expected_outcome: Understanding of Rec.709 standards, gamma tagging, and ambient viewing conditions.

lessons.what_is_taught: The reality and limitations of Look Up Tables (LUTs): 1D vs 3D LUTs, technical camera conversion LUTs vs creative styling LUTs, correct LUT placement in node trees, adjusting LUT key output opacity, and why LUTs do not replace color grading skills.
subtopics: What a LUT actually is: a mathematical lookup table mapping input RGB values to output RGB values
1D LUTs (tonal contrast only) vs 3D LUTs (complex color, hue, and saturation mapping)
Technical conversion LUTs (e.g. S-Log3 to Rec.709) vs creative aesthetic styling LUTs
Where to place LUTs: why technical balance and exposure must occur BEFORE the LUT in the node tree
Adjusting LUT intensity using the Node Key Output Gain slider to avoid heavy-handed looks
The hard truth: why relying on downloaded internet LUTs produces broken, clipping images
lessons.what_learner_does: Places a creative LUT in a dedicated node, adjusts its opacity, and corrects exposure upstream.
lessons.why_it_matters: Professional colorists use LUTs as subtle creative accents, never as an uncalibrated shortcut.
lessons.expected_outcome: Technical mastery of LUT mechanics, appropriate node placement, and opacity tuning.

lessons.what_is_taught: Developing intentional creative grades: warm commercial look, cool cinematic thriller look, clean high-key brand aesthetic, low-key dramatic mood, split-toning (warm highlights / cool shadows), contrast curve sculpting, and narrative emotional alignment.
subtopics: Deconstructing cinematic film looks: color contrast, tonal separation, and shadow roll-off
Designing a warm commercial look: golden skin highlights and rich amber midtones
Designing a cool cinematic dramatic look: teal/cyan shadows, desaturated foliage, clean highlights
Clean high-key brand look: open airy shadows, pristine whites, and vibrant saturated accents
Low-key dramatic look: crushed dark backgrounds, directional rim lights, and muted colors
Aligning the creative grade with the director's narrative brief and brand identity
lessons.what_learner_does: Develops two distinct creative grades (warm commercial and cool dramatic) from the same source clip.
lessons.why_it_matters: Creative look development gives films their distinct emotional resonance and visual signature.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to conceptualize, design, and execute distinct creative grades tailored to briefs.

lessons.what_is_taught: Protecting and perfecting human skin tones: white balance influence, Vectorscope skin-tone line, hue range isolation, adjusting skin exposure and saturation, handling natural skin variation, and avoiding artificial 'plastic' skin smoothing.
subtopics: The universal biology of human skin: blood flow creates consistent hue angles on the Vectorscope
Using the Vectorscope skin-tone indicator line as an objective hue guide
How incorrect white balance corrupts skin tones (green/magenta or orange/blue shifts)
Isolating skin with HSL qualifiers and Power Windows to adjust exposure and saturation independently
Preserving natural tonal variation: avoiding flat, single-color plastic skin masks
Harmonizing skin tones across diverse subjects under challenging mixed lighting
lessons.what_learner_does: Isolates and harmonizes skin tones across an actor's face, aligning hue precisely to the Vectorscope line.
lessons.why_it_matters: Viewers are hyper-sensitive to human skin; unnatural skin immediately destroys visual credibility.
lessons.expected_outcome: Mastery of skin tone evaluation, isolation, color harmony, and natural preservation.

lessons.what_is_taught: Managing look iterations and client presentations: Gallery Still albums, saving Version 1 vs Version 2 on clips, local vs remote versions, split-screen client comparisons, and guiding stakeholders to approved grades.
subtopics: Creating multiple grade versions on a single clip (Version 1, Version 2, Version 3)
Switching versions dynamically using keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl/Cmd+N and Ctrl/Cmd+B)
Local Versions vs Remote Versions: linking grades across all instances of a clip in the project
Organizing Gallery Still albums into categorized look books for client presentation
Split-screen and wipe comparisons: presenting look options side-by-side to clients
Professional communication: articulating creative rationale to guide client sign-off
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates three distinct local versions on a sequence and presents them in a split-screen comparison.
lessons.why_it_matters: Clients always demand options; smooth versioning makes reviews efficient and collaborative.
lessons.expected_outcome: Fluency in local/remote versioning, gallery still management, and client presentation.

lessons.what_is_taught: Introduction to High Dynamic Range (HDR) video concepts: SDR vs HDR capabilities, wider color gamuts (Rec.2020), peak luminance (1000 nits vs 100 nits), tone mapping, HDR monitoring hardware requirements, and Studio-specific mastering limitations.
subtopics: What is High Dynamic Range: extending peak brightness and retaining shadow detail simultaneously
Peak brightness: standard SDR (100 nits) vs consumer HDR (600–1000 nits) vs master mastering monitors
Major HDR delivery standards: HDR10 (static metadata), HDR10+, and Dolby Vision (dynamic metadata)
Hardware requirements: why consumer 'HDR' monitors cannot be used for critical mastering
Tone mapping: how HDR content is scaled down gracefully for standard SDR screens
Studio-specific features: understanding what HDR mastering tools require DaVinci Resolve Studio
lessons.what_learner_does: Analyzes HDR vs SDR waveforms and evaluates tone mapping responses in Resolve.
lessons.why_it_matters: Understanding HDR concepts prepares colorists for modern industry trends without false promises.
lessons.expected_outcome: Accurate theoretical literacy in HDR concepts, monitor requirements, and SDR differences.

lessons.what_is_taught: Rigorous quality assurance for color grades: verifying project-wide color management, cross-checking shot-to-shot contrast and saturation, inspecting export color tags, monitor limitations, and final client sign-off.
subtopics: Conducting an end-to-end color management audit: verifying that every clip has proper input transforms
Scrubbing the timeline with the Vectorscope open to identify sudden saturation spikes
Auditing contrast uniformity across hard cuts: ensuring blacks and whites don't bounce wildly
Testing video playback across multiple real-world consumer displays (laptop, phone, tablet)
Verifying export color space and gamma tags in QuickTime and VLC media players
Final colorist sign-off checklist before passing projects to the Fairlight audio page
lessons.what_learner_does: Performs a systematic color consistency audit across a completed 10-shot scene.
lessons.why_it_matters: A final consistency check eliminates embarrassing color discrepancies before client delivery.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to conduct comprehensive technical and visual color consistency audits.

Audio track types: Mono, Stereo, 5.1 Surround, and Adaptive multi-channel tracks
The Fairlight Mixer: input gain, EQ, dynamics, pan, fader, and mute/solo controls
Adjusting clip gain waveforms directly in the timeline vs using track faders
Understanding decibel meters: Peak meters, RMS, and true peak monitoring
Control Room panel: adjusting listening monitor levels without affecting the master mix output
lessons.what_learner_does: Configures the Fairlight interface, adjusts clip gain levels, and navigates audio tracks in the mixer.

Trimming dead silence between spoken phrases to eliminate ambient hiss jumps
Applying micro-crossfades (4–10 frames) to eliminate digital audio clicks at cut points
Room tone: capturing ambient room noise and looping it under dialogue gaps for seamless continuity
Level consistency: matching dialogue volumes across different speakers and mic setups
Manual repair awareness in Resolve Free (without relying on Studio-only AI plugins)
lessons.what_learner_does: Cleans up a noisy interview dialogue track, inserts room tone, and applies smooth audio crossfades.
lessons.why_it_matters: Clean, consistent dialogue is the foundation of professional post-production audio.

lessons.what_is_taught: Equalization (EQ) fundamentals on Fairlight: Fairlight 4-band / 6-band Parametric EQ, High-Pass (low cut) filtering, tonal balancing, improving dialogue clarity, removing low-frequency boom, notch filtering resonance, and avoiding harsh over-processing.

Opening the Fairlight track EQ: band selection (High Pass, Low Shelf, Bell, High Shelf)
Applying High-Pass filters (80Hz–100Hz) to eliminate mic rumbles, wind, and HVAC hum
Notching out irritating resonant room frequencies using high Q-factor narrow bells
Gentle mid-range boosts (2kHz–4kHz) to enhance speech articulation and presence
The golden rule of EQ: cut narrow, boost wide, and keep adjustments subtle
lessons.what_learner_does: Applies a High-Pass filter and shapes a 4-band parametric EQ to improve dialogue clarity.
lessons.why_it_matters: Proper EQ removes muddy frequencies and makes speech instantly intelligible.

lessons.what_is_taught: Dynamics processing for video finishing: Fairlight Dynamics panel, Compressor parameters (Threshold, Ratio, Attack, Release), Make-up Gain, Limiter fundamentals, and achieving consistent broadcast-standard dialogue levels.

Compressor mechanics: Threshold (activation point) and Ratio (amount of gain reduction)
Attack (speed of clamping down) and Release (speed of letting go) for natural vocal sound
Make-up Gain: restoring overall signal volume after compression reduces peaks
The Limiter: brickwall ceiling protection preventing digital distortion at 0dBFS
Targeting optimal gain reduction: aiming for 2dB to 4dB of subtle, transparent vocal compression
lessons.what_learner_does: Configures Fairlight dynamics compression on a dialogue track to achieve uniform speech volume.
lessons.why_it_matters: Compression ensures dialogue remains audible whether played on phone speakers or home theatres.
lessons.expected_outcome: Mastery of Fairlight compressor and limiter settings for controlled speech dynamics.

Creating dedicated Submix buses: Bus 1 (Dialogue), Bus 2 (Music), Bus 3 (SFX)
Routing individual timeline tracks to their designated submix buses
Applying master processing to entire stems (e.g. compressing all dialogue on the dialogue bus)
Main output bus mastering: final limiter protection and loudness monitoring
Muting and soloing submix stems during review to check individual mix layers
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates Dialogue, Music, and SFX submix buses and routes all timeline audio tracks logically.
lessons.why_it_matters: Submix routing enables global control over music beds without adjusting dozens of individual clips.
lessons.expected_outcome: Ability to route audio tracks through submix buses to a master output bus.

lessons.what_is_taught: Balancing multiple audio elements: music bed volume, dialogue priority, keyframed volume automation, manual audio ducking, sound effects placement, and acoustic continuity.
subtopics: The hierarchy of audio: spoken dialogue always holds 100% priority over background music
Establishing proper level relationships: dialogue (-12dB to -6dB) vs background music (-24dB to -18dB)
Manual audio ducking: dipping music volume under spoken dialogue using automation keyframes
Layering sound effects (whooshes, UI clicks, ambient Foley) to support on-screen visual cuts

faq.question: Is DaVinci Resolve suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. This course begins with project setup, media management and editing fundamentals before progressing into professional colour correction, grading and finishing.

faq.question: Is DaVinci Resolve Free enough for this course?
faq.answer: Yes. All compulsory learning activities and portfolio deliverables are designed to be achievable using supported features in DaVinci Resolve Free.

faq.question: What will I learn?
faq.answer: You will learn video editing, node-based colour correction, colour scopes, shot matching, colour management, creative grading, Fairlight audio finishing and professional export workflows.

faq.question: Will I learn cinematic colour grading?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to correct footage, develop creative looks, maintain shot consistency and prepare appropriate SDR deliverables.

faq.question: Will I learn node-based grading?
faq.answer: Yes. The course teaches node structure, serial nodes, primary and secondary corrections, Power Windows and practical grading organization.

faq.question: Will I learn colour management?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn Log concepts, colour spaces, Resolve Color Management, Color Space Transform and Rec.709 delivery fundamentals.

faq.question: What portfolio work will I complete?
faq.answer: You will create a 60–90-second finished video, a six-shot colour-matching exercise, two creative looks from the same footage, a Fairlight audio correction demonstration and an editable project archive with colour breakdowns.

faq.question: Will I learn Fairlight audio editing?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn dialogue cleanup, EQ, compression, music balancing, audio buses and quality-control fundamentals.

faq.question: Does the course cover Fusion?
faq.answer: It includes introductory Fusion titles, basic nodes and compositing awareness. Advanced Fusion VFX is outside the course scope.

faq.question: Will I learn AI tools?
faq.answer: The course introduces Studio-specific AI tools where available, but they are optional. Mandatory assignments focus on reliable Free-version workflows.

faq.question: Is DaVinci Resolve Studio included in the fee?
faq.answer: Do not claim Studio licensing is included unless Nova Skills has explicitly verified the applicable license arrangements.

faq.question: Do I need previous video-editing experience?
faq.answer: Basic video-editing concepts are recommended, but prior DaVinci Resolve experience is not required.

faq.question: What is the difference between Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve?
faq.answer: Both support professional editing. This course specifically emphasizes DaVinci Resolve's node-based colour correction, colour management and integrated finishing workflow.

faq.question: Will I receive editable projects?
faq.answer: Students are required to create and submit editable Resolve projects, appropriately organized media, comparison evidence and delivery documentation.

faq.question: What is the course duration and fee?
faq.answer: Eight weeks, 64 guided learning hours and ₹9,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.
